newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler to launch export sales in Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler to launch export sales in Egypt.

text.p: Chrysler Corp said Monday it will begin exporting fully-assembled vehicles from its U.S. and European manufacturing facilities to Egypt this month.
The first vehicles to arrive will be the Neon sedan, Voyager and Grand Voyager minivans and the Jeep Grand Cherokee, Chrysler said.

The three imported models will complement sales of the Jeep Cherokee, which Chrysler has been assembling locally in Egypt since the late 1980s, through a joint venture with the state-owned Arab Organization for Industrialization.

To support the expanded product offering, Chrysler said it is establishing a wholly-owned subsidiary, Chrysler Egypt, with headquarters in Cairo. The new office will handle sales, marketing, customer warranty, parts and service support for all Chrysler products in Egypt.

Chrysler sold 1,900 Jeep Cherokee vehicles in Egypt in 1996. With the introduction of imports, the company said Chrysler Egypt expects to sell a total of 2,700 to 3,000 units in its first year of operation.

"We see important opportunities for our products in the growing Egyptian automotive market, which is expected to exceed 100,000 units by the turn of the century," said Ed Brust, general manager of Chrysler Latin America, Middle East and Africa Operations. "This move is another step in our international strategy to expand our presence in fast-growing markets."
